name: Kinetic Statement Card
summary: A short headline builds word by word on a clean background, sometimes with one word or chip that cycles through options or a small icon that supports it. The scene states one idea loudly between demos: the hook, the problem, the mechanism or the outcome.
when_to_use: To open the video or a new section with one clear claim.
To name a problem or a payoff in words before showing it in the product.
When a list of things the product covers can be shown as one phrase with a cycling slot.

slots.name: headline
slots.what: one short claim, one or two lines

slots.name: emphasis_word
slots.what: the word that gets an underline, colour or weight change

slots.name: cycling_options
slots.what: a short list of words or chips that swap in one slot of the phrase

slots.name: support_visual
slots.what: a small icon, logo or illustration that pops in near the text

slots.name: background
slots.what: a plain light or dark field, optionally with soft drifting shapes

steps: Start on the empty background, with motion beginning almost immediately.
The headline reveals word by word or line by line from a mask.
An emphasis touch lands: an underline draws on or one word changes colour.
Optionally a slot in the phrase cycles through options, or icons pop in beside the text.
The text resolves to its final state and holds briefly.
The card clears or reframes to make room for the next scene.

build.gsap: One timeline per card: split the headline into words and tween each from a masked offset or low opacity with a short stagger and an expo or power ease-out; draw any underline with a stroke-dashoffset tween; for a cycling slot, chain y and blur tweens that swap the label on the beat; finish with a scale and translate tween on the text group to clear or reframe.
build.remotion: A Sequence per card; each word's opacity and translate come from a spring offset by its index times a small frame delay; a cycling chip uses child Sequences per option with a spring slide in and out; a closing interpolate on scale and position hands off to the next scene.

sound: Often an unlabelled or reverse-swoosh hit as the text builds, with a soft impact on the key word and music carrying the rest; chimes appear in a few videos. No single dependable cue.
caveats: First-motion timing comes from a minority of shots and videos.
Some members run several type cards and even a short UI moment inside one shot, so the mix is broad.
Nearly half of sound cues are unlabelled, so SFX timing is weak.
